My League

Lineup, waivers, trades, and your matchup.

Link or update your league

ESPN

Paste a link to any page of your league from the ESPN site or app (My Team works, and its link tells BFF which team is yours), or just the league ID. BFF reads every team, roster and record plus your lineup and scoring settings from ESPN.

Private league? Bring it in from ESPN in three steps

Browsers keep your ESPN sign-in to ESPN's own pages, so when BFF asks ESPN for a private league, ESPN answers as if you were signed out, even when you are signed in. These steps use ESPN's own page instead. Your league is saved in this browser (and in your BFF account, if you have one), as with any linked league.

  1. Paste your league link in the box above, then open your league's data on ESPN. Be signed in to ESPN in this browser. The page is a wall of text: that is your league.
  2. Copy all of it: Ctrl+A, then Ctrl+C (⌘A, ⌘C on a Mac). On a phone, press and hold the text, tap Select All, then Copy. In Firefox, open the Raw Data tab and press Copy.
  3. Come back here, paste it in this box and press Import.

On a computer, one click instead: drag this button to your bookmarks bar, open your league on ESPN (signed in), and click the bookmark. It sends your league straight to BFF. BFF: import from ESPN

The league manager can also make the league viewable to the public in ESPN's league settings (then the link alone is enough), or you can copy the rosters page in under Yahoo & others.

Sleeper

Type your Sleeper username to pick one of your leagues, or paste the league ID (the long number in the league's web address). BFF finds your team and keeps the rosters up to date.

Can't connect? Paste the pages instead
Type the league ID above for links to the three pages.

Yahoo, NFL.com, CBS, anything else

  1. On your league's website, open a team's roster (on Yahoo, click the team's name). A page with every team's roster works too.
  2. Select everything on the page (Ctrl+A, or ⌘A on a Mac), copy, paste it here and press Read page. BFF finds the team's name and its players; you can fix any name.
  3. Do the same for each team, then press Import.

On a phone, take screenshots of each team's roster instead (two or three per team is fine) and press Screenshots.

Starting lineup

Kickers and team defenses come along with your league: BFF projects them, sets them in your league's spots for them and counts them in the power rankings. They stay out of trade values, trade ideas and waiver targets.

Draft settings

Draft board

Draft guide by pick

Who should be there at each of your picks (by consensus market rank, the best stand-in for average draft position), our favorite targets among them, and which position dries up before your next turn.

Draft tips

Draft the cliff, not the rank

Take the position that drops off the most before your next pick. The draft guide shows that drop on every round.

Wait on a quarterback in 1-QB leagues

The 12th quarterback scores close to the 5th, and every team starts only one, so running backs and receivers fall off much faster. In superflex, quarterbacks go early.

Draft for the lineup you will start

BFF value counts the points a player adds over the best player at his position who would not start in a league your size, plus 15% over the waiver wire (VORP), so depth gets its due without overrating backups.

Set your scoring first

TE premium, 6-point passing touchdowns and other rules change who to take. Pick Custom under Scoring and every ranking, value and draft pick re-scores.

Spin Draft

Spin the machine for a random NFL team and season (1999 to last season). Draft one of that team's real fantasy scorers into an open spot: QB, RB, RB, WR, WR, TE and a FLEX (RB, WR or TE). Seven spins, seven players, the highest total wins. Points are each player's regular-season total for that team that year. Two re-spins per game; a spin with nobody who fits your open spots is free to redo. Each player can only be drafted once.

Data: nflverse weekly player stats, added up by team and season (a player traded midseason counts for each team with the points he scored there). Standard scoring: 0.04 a passing yard, 4 a passing TD, -2 an interception, 0.1 a rushing or receiving yard, 6 a rushing, receiving or return TD, 2 a two-point conversion, -2 a lost fumble; PPR adds 1 a catch, half PPR 0.5.

Fantasy Help

Your in-season toolkit: weekly calls, trends, matchups, waivers and trades, the trade analyzer and betting lines, all built from our tested data.

How to use this page
Buy & sell

Compares a player's fantasy points with what his usage (targets, carries, red-zone touches) normally produces. Big gaps tend to close: underperformers bounce back, overperformers cool off.

Usage

Risers and fallers show sudden role changes over the last two games, with the share of that change that has typically stuck. A role change matters more than one big game.

Matchups

Points each defense allows to each position, pulled toward average early in the season, and which players get the best and worst draws this week.

Schedules

How easy upcoming opponents are: the next 4 weeks for trades and pickups, the rest of the season, and playoff weeks 15 to 17 for the stretch run.

Best bets

Where the signals agree. One signal is a hint; two pointing the same way is a move.

Buy low

Scoring well below what his targets and carries usually produce. Players like this have tended to bounce back. Fill-ins whose starter is coming back, two-game samples, players losing snaps and players whose usage is already top 6 are left off.

Sell high

Scoring well above what his usage usually produces, often on touchdowns or big plays. That has tended to fade.

Usage vs. production

Each dot is a player: usage (what his targets and carries usually produce) across, actual points up. Above the dashed line he is outscoring his usage (likely to cool off); below it he is due to bounce back. Tap a dot to open the player.

Risers

Usage jumped over his last two games. Shown with the share that has typically held.

Fallers

Usage dropped over his last two games. Shown with the share that has typically held.

Best matchups this week

Toughest matchups this week

Defense vs. position

PPR points allowed per game this season. Green = gives up a lot (good for your players), red = stingy. Rank 1 is the toughest defense, 32 the easiest. Early in the season these swing, so projections use a version pulled toward average.

Gives up a lot: start your guysAverageStingy: lower expectations

Strength of schedule

How friendly each team's upcoming opponents are for that position: the next 4 weeks (best for trades and pickups), the rest of the season, and fantasy playoff weeks 15 to 17. Positive = easier than average, based on points each defense allows.

Playoff schedule winners

Startable players with the friendliest matchups in fantasy playoff weeks 15 to 17.

Playoff schedule losers

Startable players facing the toughest playoff-week defenses for their position.

Proof: how these signals did in past seasons

Every signal on this page was checked against 2021-25 results before it was used. These are the averages for players the signals flagged.

Weekly calls PPR

Every week BFF makes four calls: must starts, must sits, buy lows and sell highs. Each call locks when the player's game kicks off and is graded automatically with official stats, so every pick we have made stays on the record.

How calls are made, locked and graded

Waiver targets for most leagues

Usually unrostered in 12-team leagues, ranked by our rest-of-season value, recent usage, and the next 4 weeks of schedule.

Trade targets for most leagues

Buy: our data likes them more than the market does. Sell: the market likes them more than our data does.

Add players to each side (typos are fine), or add only one side and press Find trades for fair offers. With your league linked, offers come from real rosters and show the effect on your lineup.

Betting help

For entertainment, 21+ where legal. These are model estimates, not guarantees, and sportsbooks build a profit margin into every price. Never bet more than you can afford to lose. Gambling problem? Call or text 1-800-GAMBLER.

These are BFF predicted lines: where PrizePicks, Underdog and sportsbooks are expected to set them. Yardage and reception lines come from ESPN's and Sleeper's public projections, scaled to where books set their lines (checked against real posted lines below); so do pass attempts, completions, rush attempts and targets. Anytime TD, 1st-half TD and interceptions are BFF's chances of 1 or more, shown with their fair odds. Passing-touchdown lines, and players neither site projects, come from BFF's own opportunity model: expected targets, carries or pass attempts times efficiency, adjusted for the Vegas team total and the defense. Lines update every 10 minutes as the sites' projections, the odds and the news move, and a line is pulled when a player is reported out. Picks are where BFF's own model disagrees with the line.
